evaluations.evidence: As a moderator, I want to create a new game by entering a name and an optional description, so that I can start inviting estimators.
evaluations.rationale: Contains only role, means and rationale; no implementation/testing/procedural notes.

evaluations.evidence: As a moderator, I want to invite estimators by giving them a URL where they can access the game, so that we can start the game.
evaluations.rationale: Pure role, means and rationale without extra implementation or procedural comments.

evaluations.evidence: As a moderator, I want to start a round by entering an item in a single multi-line text field, so that we can estimate it.
evaluations.rationale: Describes role, the means of input and rationale; although UI-specific, it is still part of the means and not an extraneous comment.

evaluations.evidence: As a moderator, I want to see all items we try to estimate this session, so that I can answer questions about the current story such as "does this include ___".
evaluations.rationale: Contains only role, means and a rationale/example; no implementation or testing hints.

evaluations.evidence: As a moderator, I want to select an item to be estimated or re-estimated, so that the team sees that item and can estimate it.
evaluations.rationale: Straight role, means and rationale with no extraneous notes.

evaluations.evidence: As a moderator, I want to add an item to the list of items to be estimated, so that so that we can be flexible and accommodate situations where we think of a new story while playing.
evaluations.rationale: Only role, means and rationale; duplication of 'so that' is a typo, not an extraneous implementation note.

evaluations.evidence: As a moderator, I want to edit an item in the list of items to be estimated, so that I can make it better reflect the team's understanding of the item.
evaluations.rationale: Contains the core elements (role, means, rationale) and no extra procedural or implementation hints.

evaluations.evidence: As a moderator, I want to delete an item from the list of items to be estimated, so that we can remove it and not estimate it.
evaluations.rationale: Simple role/means/rationale structure without additional notes.

evaluations.evidence: As a moderator, I want to show all estimates immediately, so that I can decide to show the estimates that have been given even though not all estimators have given their estimate.
evaluations.rationale: Describes desired behavior and reason; no extraneous implementation or testing instructions.

evaluations.evidence: As a moderator, I want to accept the average of all estimates, so that we can move on to the next item when we agree.
evaluations.rationale: Contains only role, means and rationale.

evaluations.evidence: As a moderator, I want to have the "estimate" field filled in automatically if all estimators show the same card, so that I can accept it more quickly.
evaluations.rationale: Specifies desired automatic behavior as part of the means; not an extraneous comment or test note.

evaluations.evidence: As a moderator, I want to enter the agreed-upon estimate, so that we can move on to the next item when we agree.
evaluations.rationale: Role, means and rationale only.

evaluations.evidence: As a moderator, I want to estimate a story we estimated earlier in the session again, so that we can give a new estimate if we feel different about the story after estimating other related stories.
evaluations.rationale: Contains only the expected story elements without implementation/testing hints.

evaluations.evidence: As a moderator, I want to import stories from a spreadsheet, so that I don't have to copy and paste each individual story.
evaluations.rationale: Describes a capability (import) and reason; no extra procedural notes.

evaluations.evidence: As a moderator, I want to copy/paste stories from a spreadsheet, so that I can get started more quickly.
evaluations.rationale: Role, means and rationale only.

evaluations.evidence: As a moderator, I want to browse through previous games, so that I can find the previous game I'm looking for.
evaluations.rationale: Simple and limited to role, means and rationale.

evaluations.evidence: As a moderator, I want to view a transcript of a game, so that I can see the stories and estimates.
evaluations.rationale: Contains only the standard story components without extra notes.

evaluations.evidence: As a moderator, I want to export a transcript of a game as a HTML file, so that I can save the stories and estimates locally.
evaluations.rationale: Specifies desired export format as part of the means; not an extraneous comment.

evaluations.evidence: As a moderator, I want to export a transcript of a game as a CSV file, so that I can further process the stories and estimates.
evaluations.rationale: Specifies format for export (means) and reason; no implementation/testing hints.

evaluations.evidence: As a moderator, I want to delete a game, so that stories and estimates for this game are no longer stored.
evaluations.rationale: Only role, means and rationale present.

evaluations.evidence: As a moderator, I want to create an account for the application by entering my name, email address, a password and a username, so that I can start using the application.
evaluations.rationale: Lists fields to enter as part of the means; this is part of the story, not an extraneous note.

evaluations.evidence: As a moderator, I want to log in using my account name and password, so that I can start using the application.
evaluations.rationale: Role, means and rationale only.

evaluations.evidence: As a moderator, I want to change my account details, so that I can keep my account details up-to-date.
evaluations.rationale: No implementation or testing notes, only core elements.

evaluations.evidence: As a moderator, I want to delete my account, so that account information and games are no longer stored.
evaluations.rationale: Simple role/means/rationale without extraneous content.

evaluations.evidence: As a moderator, I want to see dates and times in my local timezone, so that I don't have to do timezone conversion myself.
evaluations.rationale: Specifies desired display behavior (means) with rationale; no extra procedural notes.

evaluations.evidence: As a moderator, I want to get a password reminder by email, so that I can get back to using the application when I've forgotten my password.
evaluations.rationale: Contains only the user goal, means and reason.

evaluations.evidence: As a moderator, I want to select whether to have the team estimate with {0, 1/2, 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, etc.} or {0, 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, etc.}, so that the team can use either the modified Fibonacci sequence or powers of 2.
evaluations.rationale: Provides choice of estimation scales as part of the means; not an extraneous implementation/test note.

evaluations.evidence: As a moderator, I want to invite up to 15 estimators, so that we can play with large but not immense teams.
evaluations.rationale: Role, means and rationale only.

evaluations.evidence: As an estimator, I want to join a game by entering my name on the page I received the URL for, so that I can participate.
evaluations.rationale: Describes user action (means) and reason without extraneous notes.

evaluations.evidence: As an estimator, I want to see the item we're estimating, so that I know what I'm giving an estimate for.
evaluations.rationale: Simple role/means/rationale structure.

evaluations.evidence: As an estimator, I want to see all items we will try to estimate this session, so that I have a feel for the sizes of the various items.
evaluations.rationale: Only contains the core user story parts.

evaluations.evidence: As a participant, I want to immediately see that an estimate has been given by a specific estimator, so that I know who has already given an estimate and who we're still waiting for.
evaluations.rationale: Describes observable behavior and rationale; no extra implementation or test instructions.

evaluations.evidence: As a participant, I want to be shown all estimates at the same time after all estimators have given their estimate, so that I can be sure estimates are independent and not influenced by other estimates given in the same draw.
evaluations.rationale: Role, means and rationale only.

evaluations.evidence: As a participant, I want to be able to change my estimate up until the last person selects a card and all are shown, so that I can change my mind based on information I hear.
evaluations.rationale: Describes allowed behavior and reason; no extraneous notes.

evaluations.evidence: As a participant, I want to be able to see each estimator's prior estimates for the story being estimated, so that I can see how his or her opinion has changed so I can ask questions.
evaluations.rationale: Only role, means and rationale present.

evaluations.evidence: As a participant, I want to see who gave what estimates during the current round, so that I know this when we're discussing the estimates.
evaluations.rationale: Contains core elements and no extraneous implementation/testing instructions.

evaluations.evidence: As a participant, I want to be able start a two-minute countdown timer that all participants can see, so that I can limit the time spent discussing the estimates when I think we've talked long enough.
evaluations.rationale: Specifies desired feature (timer) and rationale; not an extraneous comment.

evaluations.evidence: As a participant, I want to have the two-minute timer reset itself as soon as we all play an estimate, so that it's ready for use on the next round.
evaluations.rationale: Desired behavior described as means with rationale; no extra notes.

evaluations.evidence: As a participant, I want to scroll back through the stories and estimates from prior rounds, so that I can use this information when I estimate the item of the current round.
evaluations.rationale: Simple role, means and rationale; no extraneous content.

evaluations.evidence: As a participant, I want to always have the cards in the same order across multiple draws, so that it's easy to compare estimates.
evaluations.rationale: Only core story elements present.

evaluations.evidence: As a participant, I want to change my estimate as long as the draw has not been completed, so that I can change my mind.
evaluations.rationale: Role, means and rationale without additional implementation/testing notes.

evaluations.evidence: As a participant, I want to have a small thumbnail photo displayed near where my cards are played, so that the game is more personal because I see who I'm estimating with.
evaluations.rationale: Specifies a UI element as means with rationale; not an extraneous comment or test instruction.

evaluations.evidence: As a developer, I want to have written a site which is compliant with XHTML and CSS standards, so that as many people as possible can access the site and view it as intended.
evaluations.rationale: Expresses quality goals (standards compliance) as part of the means/rationale; no extraneous procedural notes.

evaluations.evidence: As a developer, I want to have a list of definitions for commonly used terms, so that everyone working on the project can understand each other more easily.
evaluations.rationale: Role, means and rationale only.

evaluations.evidence: As a developer, I want to have created database indexes, so that the queries run as fast as possible.
evaluations.rationale: Developer task describing implementation outcome, but it is presented as role/means/rationale without extraneous notes.

evaluations.evidence: As a developer, I want to have the application function correctly in Internet Explorer 6 and 7, Firefox 1.5 and 2, and Safari 2, so that as many people as possible can fully use the application.
evaluations.rationale: Specifies target browsers as part of the means; not an extraneous comment or test instruction.

evaluations.evidence: As a developer, I want to have the site comply with the W3C accessibility guidelines where possible, so that people with accessibility issues can use the application.
evaluations.rationale: Accessibility requirement is stated as part of the means/rationale; no extra notes.

evaluations.evidence: As a user, I want to have the application respond quickly to my actions, so that I don't get bored.
evaluations.rationale: Contains only role, desired behavior and rationale.

evaluations.evidence: As a user, I want to be able to use Unicode, so that I can use any language I like.
evaluations.rationale: Role, means and rationale only.

evaluations.evidence: As a user, I want to see sensible and predictable URLs, so that the application feels logical and transparent.
evaluations.rationale: Only core story components present; no extraneous implementation or testing notes.

evaluations.evidence: As a user, I want to have nice error pages when something goes wrong, so that I can trust the system and its developers.
evaluations.rationale: Describes desired user-facing behavior and reason without extra procedural details.

evaluations.evidence: As a Researcher, I want results to be stored in a non-identifiable way, so that I can study the data to see things like whether estimates converged around the first opinion given by "estimator A" for example.
evaluations.rationale: Specifies data anonymization requirement and example rationale; no implementation/test instructions.

evaluations.evidence: As a Mike, I want to be able to see some metrics on use of the game, so that I can see how much it is being used.
evaluations.rationale: Contains role, means and rationale only (role is a named stakeholder), with no extraneous notes.
